references.text: Caleb silenced the people and encouraged them to go up and take possession of the land, reflecting the command to 'go up and take possession' in Deuteronomy 1:21.
Moses and Joshua urge the people not to fear the inhabitants of the land, paralleling 'do not be afraid or discouraged' in Deuteronomy 1:21.
God's promise to Abraham to give the land to his descendants, which is the basis for the expression 'the Lord your God has given you the land'.
God's promise to Isaac to give the lands to his offspring, a confirmation of the promise made to the fathers mentioned in Deuteronomy 1:21.
God's promise to Jacob regarding the land, confirming 'as the Lord, the God of your fathers, has promised you'.
The Lord commands Joshua to be strong and courageous, not to fear or be discouraged, the same encouragement found in Deuteronomy 1:21.
The Lord promises to give Joshua and Israel the land He swore to their ancestors, paralleling the promise mentioned in Deuteronomy 1:21.
Moses encourages the people to be strong and courageous, not to fear, for the Lord goes with them—the same message as in Deuteronomy 1:21.
Moses tells Joshua that the Lord goes before him and that he should not fear or be discouraged, an identical exhortation to that in Deuteronomy 1:21.
The Lord urges His people not to fear, for He is with them—the same comfort and encouragement as in Deuteronomy 1:21.
